awd_titl_txt: Conference: WORKSHOP: Doctoral Consortium at Student Research Workshop at the Nations of Americas Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics
awd_abstract_narration:
The Association for Computational Linguistics (ACL) is the primary international scientific organization in the fields of computational linguistics, natural language processing and human language technologies. The annual meeting of its Nations of the Americas chapter (NAACL) is one of the most prestigious and selective international conferences in these fields. The Student Research Workshop (SRW) is an established tradition at NAACL conferences, allowing students to present their research and receive feedback from more senior researchers. It provides a valuable opportunity for students at different stages of their academic careers. This grant supports student participation at the NAACL-HLT 2025 Student Research Workshop, which will take place during the main NAACL-HLT conference in Albuquerque, New Mexico from April 29 to May 4, 2025.

Student participants will submit to present either a thesis proposal to receive feedback or a research paper which describes completed work, or work in progress with preliminary results. Additionally, there will be a pre-submission mentoring program, which enables students submitting to the SRW to first get feedback on their work from a post-PhD expert in their field. Undergraduate and graduate students at the early stages of their graduate career get a chance to present their work and receive feedback before it becomes suitable for publication at the main conference. The SRW also provides valuable experience for the student organizers, who are directly involved in recruiting reviewers, managing the review process and running the workshop.  Overall, the opportunities for interaction with other students and with senior researchers will positively influence the student participants and will likely inspire many to devote further effort to academic studies and careers.

This award reflects NSF's statutory mission and has been deemed worthy of support through evaluation using the Foundation's intellectual merit and broader impacts review criteria.

por.por_cntn:
This award supported student participation in the Student Research Workshop (SRW) held at the 2025 Annual Conference of the Nations of Americas Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics (NAACL-HLT 2025) in Albuquerque, New Mexico, from April 29 to May 4, 2025. The SRW is a long-standing venue that gives students the opportunity to present their research in computational linguistics, natural language processing, and human language technologies, and to receive constructive feedback from established researchers in these fields.

Intellectual Merit: With support from this grant, 14 student authors and 2 student organizers from U.S. universities were able to attend and participate in the workshop. Student authors presented work spanning a range of topics in natural language processing and computational linguistics, including both completed research papers and thesis proposals describing work in progress. By presenting at the SRW, these students contributed new ideas and preliminary findings to the research community while also subjecting their work to rigorous peer review. A pre-submission mentoring program paired students with post-doctoral experts who provided detailed feedback on drafts before the formal review process, strengthening the quality of the submitted work and helping students develop stronger research methodologies. The workshop thus served as both a venue for disseminating new research and a mechanism for improving the caliber of student scholarship in the field.

Broader Impacts: The SRW plays an important role in workforce development for science and technology. The grant funded travel and registration costs, enabling students to attend one of the premier conferences in their field. Attendance at NAACL-HLT 2025 gave funded students access to the full main conference program, including keynote talks, tutorials, and workshops, as well as informal networking opportunities with peers and senior researchers from academia and industry worldwide.

The two funded student organizers gained hands-on experience in the logistics of running a scientific workshop, including recruiting reviewers, managing the peer review process, and coordinating the event itself. These organizational and leadership skills complement the students' technical training and prepare them for future roles in the research community.

The mentoring component of the SRW deserves particular emphasis as a broader impact. By connecting early-career students with experienced researchers before the formal submission deadline, the program strengthened the quality of student work and helped participants build professional networks that will support their long-term development as researchers.

Overall, this award enabled 16 U.S.-based students to participate meaningfully in a top-tier international research venue. The experience of presenting work, receiving expert feedback, and engaging with the broader research community is expected to have a lasting positive effect on these students' academic development and career trajectories in science and engineering.
